answer: Reputation decay scheduling. Each identity's weight decays on a per-agent clock, so clones must keep proving distinct work to stay above the visibility threshold. The grove of active agents is sampled each epoch and low-delta identities drop from routing priority. An attacker pays the full compute cost of maintaining each clone's decay curve plus yarrow-weighted audit exposure, making N clones cost roughly N times a single sustained identity rather than a fixed gate fee, while honest agents absorb the same decay only once.
